sections.title: Manufacturing
sections.subtitle: Connect production, quality and maintenance with enterprise systems and governed operational insight.

sections.heading: Connect manufacturing with the enterprise
sections.body:
Production plans, quality records and maintenance decisions often sit in separate applications. Linkfields combines enterprise platforms, application integration, automation and governed analytics to connect the information teams need.

We define interfaces and ownership between business applications and shop-floor systems before designing change. Operational technology (OT), equipment control and industrial safety remain outside any assumed scope; supported interfaces and responsibilities must be agreed.

sections.heading: What we deliver
sections.description: Four connected workflows, with decision rights and operating boundaries agreed before delivery.

items.title: Production and business planning
items.description: When demand, capacity and stock plans diverge, connect ERP orders and planning data into a reviewable forecast and schedule.
items.bullets:
Workflow – planners review assumptions and approve changes.
Output – shared planning views and a documented exception queue.
items.footText: Forecast error and planning rework against an agreed baseline.

items.title: Execution visibility and ERP integration
items.description: When progress updates require manual reconciliation, connect agreed production-status sources with ERP and operational applications.
items.bullets:
Boundary – read and exchange approved data; no assumed equipment control.
Output – interface contracts, reconciled status and failed-message handling.
items.footText: Status freshness, reconciliation effort and integration exceptions.

items.title: Quality records and exceptions
items.description: When quality evidence is scattered, connect inspection records, document approvals and corrective-action routing.
items.bullets:
Control – quality teams review exceptions and retain disposition authority.
Output – traceable records and an agreed approval workflow.
items.footText: Record completeness, approval time and exception rework.

items.title: Asset maintenance and supply insight
items.description: When asset history and spare-parts availability are disconnected, combine equipment, maintenance and inventory data for planning.
items.bullets:
Prerequisite – usable history, known data freshness and model validation.
Control – maintenance teams approve interventions; suppliers remain connected through agreed interfaces.
items.footText: Maintenance planning accuracy and parts-availability exceptions.

sections.heading: Manufacturing software and accelerators
sections.description: Select software and reusable IP around your manufacturing requirements; validate fit with your systems and data during discovery.

items.title: Linkworks
items.description: Composable operational applications, REST APIs and UI where ERP or CRM does not fit. Tailor workflows around existing enterprise systems.

items.title: Digital Twin Suite
items.description: Reusable IP for equipment failure prediction, forecasting simulation and inventory optimisation. Validate models on the assets and history in scope.

items.title: Predictive Analytics Suite
items.description: Demand-forecasting IP to support planning. Agree source data, evaluation periods and planner review before operational use.

items.title: testoriumz
items.description: Low-code software testing, AI root-cause analysis and CI/CD integration for operational application releases, not manufactured-product inspection.

items.title: Delivery accelerators
items.description: Modernisation, integration, migration and regression packs for controlled platform change. Tailor interfaces, reconciliation and release gates to scope.

sections.note: Products are available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without services. Reusable accelerators are tailored within delivery.

sections.heading: Start with your production or maintenance requirements
sections.description: Prioritise the workflow, systems and operational decisions in scope. Agree discovery outputs and measurable acceptance criteria before committing to implementation.

items.title: Map the production-to-enterprise flow
items.description: An example engagement starts with the process, ERP and approved shop-floor interfaces. Define data contracts, owners and a read/write boundary.
items.bullets:
Artefacts – workflow map and integration architecture
Decisions – plant scope, dependencies and responsibility matrix

items.title: Agree quality and acceptance gates
items.description: Assess data readiness, review predictive models and test application changes before release. Operational teams retain quality and maintenance decisions.
items.bullets:
Artefacts – validation plan, regression evidence and release checklist
Measures – baseline, evaluation period and acceptance criteria

items.title: Choose a delivery model
items.description: Use Fixed Price for defined scope, Time & Materials for evolving discovery, or a Dedicated Team for sustained engineering. Discuss Managed Service for ongoing application needs.

sections.note: Describe the process and existing systems, not sensitive plant or control-system details. We can agree an NDA before sharing confidential information.
